title: Inversion for Dramatic Effect
completion_message: ¡Soberbio! La Inversión Negativa (Negative Inversion) es el sello distintivo del inglés retórico más culto. Cuando usas estructuras como 'Not only did we win' o 'Under no circumstances should you', comandas la atención de toda la sala de juntas.

parts.visual:
En inglés formal escrito o en discursos persuasivos, ponemos ciertas palabras negativas o restrictivas al principio de la oración para dar énfasis. 
¡Cuando hacemos esto, el sujeto y el verbo auxiliar se INVIERTEN (como en una pregunta)!

1. Not only... but also (No solo... sino también): 
Normal: We not only won the contract, but we also got a bonus. 
Inversión: NOT ONLY DID WE WIN the contract, but we also got a bonus. 
(Nota: Se usa el auxiliar 'did' porque 'won' es pasado simple).
parts.audio: Welcome to Negative Inversion. In formal English or persuasive speeches, we place negative or restrictive words at the beginning of the sentence for dramatic emphasis. When we do this, the subject and the auxiliary verb are INVERTED, exactly like a question format! Number 1: Not only... but also. Normal sentence: We not only won the contract, but we also got a bonus. With inversion: NOT ONLY DID WE WIN the contract, but we also got a bonus. Notice we use the auxiliary 'did'.

parts.visual:
Más estructuras de Inversión (Sujeto y Auxiliar invertidos): 

2. Under no circumstances (Bajo ninguna circunstancia): 
Normal: You should not sign this contract under any circumstances. 
Inversión: UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCES SHOULD YOU sign this contract. 

3. Scarcely... when / Hardly... when / No sooner... than (Apenas... cuando): 
Inversión: HARDLY HAD HE ARRIVED when the meeting started. 
Inversión: NO SOONER HAD SHE SPOKEN than the alarm went off. 

4. Little did I know (Poco sabía yo / No tenía idea): 
Inversión: LITTLE DID WE KNOW that the company was going bankrupt. 

5. Never before / Seldom / Rarely (Nunca antes / Rara vez): 
Inversión: RARELY HAVE I SEEN such dedication.
parts.audio: More Inversion structures. Number 2: Under no circumstances. Normal: You should not sign this contract under any circumstances. Inversion: UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCES SHOULD YOU sign this contract. Number 3: Scarcely, Hardly, and No sooner. These mean 'just after'. Inversion: HARDLY HAD HE ARRIVED when the meeting started. Or: NO SOONER HAD SHE SPOKEN than the alarm went off. Number 4: Little did I know. Inversion: LITTLE DID WE KNOW that the company was going bankrupt. Number 5: Never before, Seldom, and Rarely. Inversion: RARELY HAVE I SEEN such dedication.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige la estructura de Inversión Negativa correcta.

questions.question: Normal: He not only lied to us, but he also stole money. -> Inversion: Not only ____ to us, but he also stole money.
questions.explanation: Auxiliar did + sujeto he + verbo base lie.

questions.question: Normal: You must not press this button under any circumstances. -> Inversion: Under no circumstances ____ this button.
questions.explanation: Under no circumstances MUST YOU PRESS.

questions.question: Normal: I have never seen such a terrible presentation. -> Inversion: Never before ____ such a terrible presentation.
Normal: She had hardly sat down when the phone rang. -> Inversion: Hardly ____ down when the phone rang.
Normal: I had no idea that they were planning a hostile takeover. -> Inversion: Little ____ that they were planning a hostile takeover.
questions.explanation: Little DID I KNOW (es una frase idiomática fija para 'no tenía idea').

questions.question: Normal: We rarely find such talented engineers. -> Inversion: Rarely ____ such talented engineers.
questions.explanation: Rarely DO WE FIND (presente simple -> auxiliar do).

questions.question: Normal: They had no sooner published the article than they were sued. -> Inversion: No sooner ____ the article than they were sued.
Normal: You can leave the office only after 5 PM. -> Inversion: Only after 5 PM ____ the office.
questions.explanation: Only after 5 PM CAN YOU LEAVE.

questions.question: Not only ____ late for the meeting, but she also forgot the report.
questions.explanation: Not only WAS SHE (el verbo to be se invierte a sí mismo).

questions.question: On no account ____ this information to the press. (Bajo ningún concepto deberías revelar).
questions.explanation: On no account SHOULD YOU REVEAL.

questions.question: Seldom ____ such a blatant disregard for safety protocols.
Scarcely ____ the building when the roof collapsed.
At no time ____ that the company was in financial trouble.
questions.explanation: At no time DID HE MENTION.

questions.question: Little ____ realize how much damage his words had caused.
Only when the CEO resigned ____ the severity of the crisis.
Not until the auditor arrived ____ the missing funds.
In no way ____ responsible for the damages.
No sooner ____ the contract than they realized their mistake.
Not only ____ our target, but we also exceeded it by 20%.
Under no circumstances ____ the firewall be disabled.
questions.explanation: Under no circumstances SHOULD the firewall be disabled (Pasiva).

stages.title: Written Expression
stages.description: Escribe las dos palabras de la inversión (auxiliar + sujeto).

questions.question: Not only (he lied) -> Not only ____ ____ lie.
Under no circumstances (you must) -> ____ ____ sign this.
Never before (I have) -> Never before ____ ____ seen this.
Hardly (she had) -> Hardly ____ ____ arrived.
Little (I knew) -> Little ____ ____ know.
Rarely (we find) -> Rarely ____ ____ find it.
No sooner (they had) -> No sooner ____ ____ left.
Not only (she was) -> Not only ____ ____ late.
At no time (he mentioned) -> At no time ____ ____ mention it.
In no way (we are) -> In no way ____ ____ responsible.

pairs.target: Poco sabía yo / No tenía idea
